label: rem:connes-distance-not-reeb-step-count
title: $d_{\mathrm{Connes}}$ is a minimal Reeb step count only in the $q \to \infty$ limit
html:
A spectral distance built from D_\nabla is often read as counting Reeb steps: the minimal number of applications of the flow needed to carry one state to another. The reading is available only in a limit, and the qualification belongs next to the identification of the Reeb coefficient rather than in a footnote to it.

The two coefficients of D_\nabla are a convex pair,

  q^{-1} \;+\; \bigl(1 - q^{-1}\bigr) \;=\; 1 ,

with q^{-1} weighting the gradient direction and \hbar_q = 1-q^{-1} the Reeb direction. A metric induced by D_\nabla therefore measures a mixture. It reduces to a pure Reeb step count exactly when the gradient share vanishes, that is as q \to \infty, where the operator becomes purely contact. At the opposite end, q = 1, the Reeb share vanishes and the operator is pure gradient --- the classical point, where there is no Reeb period at all.

At the substrate parameter the mixture is lopsided in the wrong direction for the step-count reading. The gradient carries 90.09\,\% of the weight and the Reeb direction 9.908\,\%, so nine parts in ten of what the metric measures is not Reeb transport. Any identification of d_{\mathrm{Connes}} with a minimal step count at q_0 would therefore be off by an order of magnitude in its dominant term, and the gap is not a small correction to be absorbed.

Two obstructions to the spectral-distance programme are in play and they are independent. The mixing above says that even a well-defined distance is not the quantity one wanted. Separately, the degeneracy obstruction says the distance built from the Markov--Gram form is not well-defined at all until the radical is quotiented away. Repairing either leaves the other standing.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall: it invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs --- real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical or q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here. The percentages above are q_0^{-1} = 0.90091828395574149216 and \hbar_{q_0} = 0.09908171604425850784.
